meta.description: Five experiments on French sentences with the anaphoric trigger aussi ('too') in if-, or- and unless-sentences, in the canonical order, where the clause that can satisfy the presupposition precedes the trigger, and the inverse order, where it follows. Experiments 1 and 4 collected inferential judgments, rating on a continuous scale from no to yes whether the conditional or the unconditional presupposition follows from a sentence; Experiments 2, 3 and 5 collected acceptability judgments, with control sentences for local accommodation with too and with the, a justified presupposition and no presupposition. Experiments 1 and 2 were run on one group of participants, 3 and 4 on a second, and 5, with complex fillers, on a third (Table 3). The tables print means and, for the inferential experiments, one-way ANOVAs comparing the two inferences; standard errors are shown only as error bars and are not recorded.

types.name: Construction
types.doc: The connective of a target sentence (§2.5, (48)–(49)).

levels.name: ifSentence
levels.label: if
levels.doc: a conditional, 'if p, qq'' or 'if not qq', not p'

levels.name: orSentence
levels.label: or
levels.doc: a disjunction, '(not p) or qq'' or 'qq' or (not p)'

levels.name: unlessSentence
levels.label: unless
levels.doc: an unless-sentence, 'unless qq', not p'; only the inverse order was tested

types.name: Order
types.doc: The order of the trigger and the clause that can satisfy its presupposition ((48)–(49)).

levels.name: canonical
levels.label: canonical
levels.doc: the satisfying clause precedes the trigger

levels.name: inverse
levels.label: inverse
levels.doc: the trigger precedes the satisfying clause

types.name: Inference
types.doc: The inference rated in the inferential judgment task ((56)).

levels.name: conditional
levels.label: conditional
levels.doc: the conditional presupposition, 'studying abroad would be stupid of Ann'

levels.name: unconditional
levels.label: unconditional
levels.doc: the unconditional presupposition, 'Ann will make a stupid decision'

types.name: Control
types.doc: The control sentences of the acceptability judgment tasks ((57)–(60)).

levels.name: localAccommodationToo
levels.label: (57) local accommodation too
levels.doc: a negated too-sentence whose presupposition must be accommodated locally

levels.name: justifiedPresupposition
levels.label: (58) justified presupposition
levels.doc: a too-sentence whose presupposition is satisfied by the preceding sentence

levels.name: localAccommodationThe
levels.label: (60) local accommodation the
levels.doc: a negated definite description whose presupposition must be accommodated locally
